# Maximum Distinct Elements After K Swaps

## Problem

## Requirements

You are given two integer arrays, `a` and `b`, both of length `n`. You may perform no more than `k` swaps, where each swap exchanges one entry from `a` with one entry from `b`. Determine the largest possible count of distinct values in `a`.

## Examples

```
n = 5
a = [5, 5, 6, 6, 7]
b = [8, 6, 9, 5, 8]
k = 2
```




Exchange `a[1]` with `b[0]`, then exchange `a[3]` with `b[2]`. This produces `a = [5, 8, 6, 9, 7]`, containing `5` unique values. Answer: `5`.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Start by identifying elements in array a that are duplicates, as swapping them out can increase distinct count.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a frequency count of each value in both arrays to decide which swaps are most beneficial, prioritizing swaps that bring in values not already present in a.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

After swapping, the maximum distinct count is limited by n (the length of a) and up to k swaps, but also by the availability of distinct values in b.

</details>
